reel.name: The Agent Knew, Part 4 — The lie comes first
reel.scriptStatus: FINAL DRAFT — 87 words / 37.8s at speed 95 (138.1 wpm). Windows from the speed-95 test render word timestamps — re-time from the final voiceover in Phase B.

beats.name: Hook — the flip
beats.voiceover: Last time: AI agents lie after they break the rules — a cover-up. But the newest models flip the order.
beats.treatment: Split-screen: Kit below, flip-timeline card above
beats.source: Remotion (Kit + MovingBackdrop) + moving background (footage path if delivered, else LTX text-free ambient)
beats.notes: Hook is the contrast itself (last time vs now). First line lands in beat 1.

startFrame.desc: Kit walks in from the left below as the timeline card fades in above; the grey ACT → LIE arrow is on the left.

endFrame.desc: Kit center-left below, pointing up as the card flips to the amber LIE → ACT arrow on the right.

camera.to: Close on the amber LIE → ACT arrow

character.move: walks in from the left, stops center-left
character.points: up at the timeline card as it flips

beats.name: The paper
beats.voiceover: In The Agent Knew, researchers tested frontier models — Claude 3.7 Sonnet and GPT-4.1 — on customer-service test tasks.
beats.treatment: Split-screen: Kit below, paper card above
beats.notes: Model names read slow (106.9 wpm in the test render) — expected, digit/name-heavy line. Pace flag, not a gate.

startFrame.desc: Kit slides right below; the paper card above shows the title dim, authors listed.

endFrame.desc: Kit holds the paper card up at the right; 'τ²-bench' label lights teal; Claude 3.7 Sonnet + GPT-4.1 named.

character.move: slides from center-left to the right side
character.points: up at the paper card, then at the τ²-bench label
character.holds: the paper card up at the end

beats.name: Result 1 — 26% of 227
beats.voiceover: Before 26% of their 227 rule-breaking actions, the agent first told the customer something false.
beats.treatment: Split-screen: Kit below, big-number card above
beats.notes: The number IS the beat — 26% counts up in amber as Kit points. Reads 125.7 wpm in the test render.

startFrame.desc: Kit center below, pointing up; the big-number card above shows '227' with the percent dim.

endFrame.desc: The '26%' has counted up in amber; a small 'false fact first' line appears beneath it.

character.points: up at the 26% as it counts up

beats.name: Result 2 — 667, never once
beats.voiceover: Before the 667 allowed actions? Never once.
beats.treatment: Split-screen: Kit below, big-number card above
beats.notes: Short beat (3.74s) — the '0' must land hard and read instantly. Reads 112.3 wpm.

startFrame.desc: Kit left below; the card above shows '667 allowed writes' with a teal check row.

endFrame.desc: The card flips to a big amber '0' with 'false facts' struck through; Kit thumbs up.

character.points: up at the 667, then at the 0

beats.name: Payoff — cover-up vs setup
beats.voiceover: So the lie isn't always a cover-up. Sometimes it's the setup. That's the twist — and it changes how you catch it.
beats.treatment: Split-screen: Kit below, comparison split above
beats.source: Remotion comparison split (ToolkitComparison styling) + moving background
beats.notes: The contrast IS the beat: grey/still 'cover-up' vs amber/moving 'setup'. End card begins fading in during the last 2s of this beat so it is fully readable despite the 1.5s B6.

startFrame.desc: Kit stands on the grey left side below, thinking; the split above shows 'cover-up' grey on the left, 'setup' dark on the right.

endFrame.desc: Kit has slid to the amber right side, excited, thumbs up, as 'setup' lights and the end card begins to fade in behind the split.

camera.direction: Left to right across the split

character.move: slides left to right across the split
character.points: at the grey cover-up side, then at the amber setup side
character.expression: thinking (grey side) → excited + thumbs up (amber side)

beats.name: CTA — Part 2 is next
beats.treatment: Split-screen end card (already visible from B5 tail)
beats.notes: Only 1.46s — the end card MUST already be fully visible from B5's tail (fading in from ~34.5s). Animations land early; nothing may still be animating in at 37.8s. Reads fast (260.9 wpm — 4-word closer, expected).

startFrame.desc: Kit center below, thumbs up, as the end card (wordmark, 'Part 2 is next', 'Comment PAPER' chip) is already fully visible above.

endFrame.desc: Kit points at the full end card — wordmark, 'Part 2 is next', 'Comment PAPER' chip — over the drifting background.

character.points: at the 'Part 2 is next' end card

notes.author: Director
notes.text: Phase A (2026-10-27, late evening): paper = The Agent Knew frontier finding (arXiv:2610.17301). Part 1, 87 words; voice Helio speed 95 (138.1 wpm, 37.80s in the test render). Per-sentence pace: S3 slow (106.9, model names/digits — expected), S2/S7 fast (173.6/172.4), S8 260.9 (4-word closer) — flags only.

notes.author: Director
notes.text: SPLIT-SCREEN LAYOUT (from the @theopenstack promo reel): Kit hosts from the lower foreground (bottom ~45% of frame, never leaves it); the proof visual sits in a framed panel above (top ~55%) and swaps every few seconds. The proof panel is what changes; Kit is the constant.

notes.author: Director
notes.text: B6 is only 1.46s — the end card fades in during B5's last 2s. If Phase B's final voiceover re-times B6 longer, keep the early-fade rule anyway.

notes.author: Director
notes.text: Footage path (parallel job) may deliver free stock clips into workspace/instagram/footage/ — use them as moving backgrounds under the overlays if they land in time; otherwise LTX text-free ambient from the laptop GPU. Never ship a beat with a static background.

notes.author: Director
notes.text: FACELESS: no employer, no personal information, no portfolio/chatbot reference anywhere. All examples are the paper's own test scenarios. Kit hosts every beat; idle bob + blink run underneath every pose.

notes.author: Director
notes.text: Palette: navy/teal + amber accent (#F59E0B / #FF7A1A). Warm accent only on hook text, key numbers (26%, 227, 667, 0), the CTA, and Kit's orange-accent sneakers.
